newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-SGB cuts debt with Union Miniere stake sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SGB cuts debt with Union Miniere stake sale.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) said on Wednesday it sold a 24 percent stake in non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere (UM) to help cut its debt to close to zero.
SGB said in a statement it sold the stake to a banking syndicate, which would place the shares with Belgian and international institutional investors.
The sale raised about 20 billion francs ($550.8 million) and would yield a capital gain of about 12 billion francs.

SGB said revenue from the stake sale would wipe out most of the debt taken on to finance the acquisition of a minority stake in Belgian utility holding company Tractebel in 1996. SGB's debt currently stand at about 20 billion francs.

An SGB spokesman told Reuters that following the sale, and if investors exchanged SGB bonds convertible into Arbed shares in December for an amount of two billion francs, SGB's debt would fall to zero at the end of 1997.
Union Miniere has been on the auction block for a long time.

Disappointing earnings at the cyclical group led SGB to reduce its UM stake from 82 percent at the end of 1992 to just over 50 percent at the start of 1995 via repeated sales to institutional investors.
SGB said on Wednesday it would hold on to 25 percent of UM's capital and would remain the leading shareholder.

As recently as March, at SGB's 1996 earnings news conference, chairman Etienne Davignon said that SGB was happy with its current portfolio and he saw no reason to change it. He also said UM would not be sold in the coming months.

Most SGB-watchers suspected that UM, along with other key SGB stakes, was for sale since SGB's French parent Suez Lyonnaise said it wanted to focus on utility services and called all other activities "non-core".
For SGB that means only its Tractebel unit, a leading Belgian utility group, is a strategic asset.
"Non-strategic" assets include Generale Bank, insurer Fortis AG, foam products group Recticel and French electronics group Sagem.
SGB chief executive officer Philippe Liotier has said both the UM and Recticel stakes were "not forever".
Asked which unit was the next one to go, an SGB spokeswoman told Reuters: "Anyone is free to make a bet on that."

UM shares were suspended on the Brussels bourse before SGB's announcement. By midsession they were 7.6 percent lower at 3,460 francs after falling nine percent to 3,410 at the start of trade, before the suspension.
The shares had soared from 2,100 francs in January to a high of 3,840 on July 7 on the back of rising zinc prices and a strong dollar.
SGB shares were down one percent at 3,695 francs. ($ = 36.31 Belgian Francs)
